ratings_why.fun: Planning the order of your funerals and watching slots refill bigger is a clear, satisfying arc, and the Wake gives the shop its own story.
ratings_why.distinct: Folding sale into death is fresh, but the fight half is a familiar death-summons-a-token tribe.

verdict_why: Sexton's shop buff and Candlesnuff's limit don't say what happens in the common case; a wording pass fixes both.

points.text: Sexton of the Litter Acre reads as an aura on the shop, so a player can't tell whether a bought unit keeps the +1/+1. Say "Units in your shop gain" or "are bought with".
With Bootlace Cordwainer, Candlesnuff Abbess's "Six times a fight" could count Fruit triggers or Sprouts made. Say which, e.g. "Sprout Fruit triggers six times a fight".
Warden Amanita doesn't say whether the unit just killed counts toward the damage. Add "counting that one" or "before it".
Print each Sprout's fixed size on it as it grows out of the dead unit, so the three counts don't all have to live in the hero frame.

Grandmother Bootlace is the founder nobody has seen all of, but her card is a plain Sprout aura. Something that reaches every slot at once would carry the fantasy, like Sprouts appearing in empty slots.

standouts.why: Clerk Inkcap writes himself away: each entry buffs a friend and shortens him. The lore is the rule.
Ludwig the lodger can't be sold and grows off the dead around him. Funny, readable, and the drawback is the joke.
Old Fingers digs up what you sold or lost, so selling in the shop pays off in the fight.

weakest.why: Crape Spinner is a plain Sprout aura with no funeral in what it does.
Foxfire Lamplighter is a generic counter reader. The glowing chapel deserves more than +1/+1 per 4.
Grandmother Bootlace is the tribe's legend, but her capstone reads like a bigger Crape Spinner.

flags.note: Unclear whether shop buffs stay on units once bought.
What "Six times a fight" counts is unclear when Cordwainer doubles Fruit.
Unclear whether the count includes the unit just killed.
Bellows on the buy-sell-Sprout loop gives a lot each turn. Capped, but worth the owner's eye.
A slot refilling many times in a long fight can read as noise without a clear grow-out animation.
